population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. ~262M US adults × 10.5% ≈ 27.5M current users (all indications). Ever 17% ≈ 44.5M, so 6.5% of adults (~17M) have used and are off now. Arithmetic: current users who are restarters ≈ 40% × 10.5 = 4.2 pp; off-now users who had already cycled once ≈ 1.0 pp; (4.2 + 1.0) / 17 ≈ 31% of ever-users have stopped and restarted, consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart. Income: the middle third (employer-insured) fell most as employer weight coverage retreated; the bottom third rose from Medicaid opt-ins and the HRSA free-provision programme; the top third is held up by cash pay. Age-weighted check (shares 20/33/24/23%): 0.8 + 2.97 + 4.32 + 2.42 ≈ 10.5. The 50–64 band fell from 22% to 18% as employer plans left the market. The 65+ band rose from 9% to 10.5% on the Medicare Bridge even with bone-density warnings, which moved older users onto lower doses rather than off the drug. Off-drug population: ~17M former users, most of whom stopped over cost or coverage, not side effects; ~60% of adults with obesity have never used. Pediatric: ~0.9% of under-18s, mostly adolescents 12–17; under-12 use following the Nov 2027 liraglutide approval for ages 6–11 is ~40k children, two-thirds on Medicaid-covered generic liraglutide.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge extended past its Dec 2027 sunset as a CMMI model through 2030: $245/month to manufacturer, $50 copay; ~2.4M beneficiaries on obesity coverage → 2.4M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.1B/yr. Medicaid: 24 states opted in at $245; ~1.5M enrollees → 1.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.4B/yr federal+state. HRSA Healthy Weight Access Program (from Apr 2028): free daily oral GLP-1 (Wegovy pill or Foundayo) at community health centres for uninsured/underinsured adults with BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with prediabetes. Federal purchase price $149/month; target 1.1M enrolled by end-2029 → 1.1M × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.0B/yr; $4B appropriated for FY2028–29. End-2028 enrolment ~0.6M. Publicly paid obesity fills ≈ 4.5M of 27.5M users (~16%).
access.generic_rest_of_world: India generics now $6–40/month across 60+ brands; Canada generic semaglutide ~CAD 70–100; Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and much of Southeast Asia have generics; WHO prequalified two generic semaglutide products in 2027. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Brand cash channels (TrumpRx, LillyDirect, NovoCare): orals $149 starting / $199–299 maintenance; injectables $199–299. Nominal list prices persist, but nobody pays them. Employer coverage for weight management is 60% → 44% (BGH-style survey, Jan 2028). Most remaining plans cover only diabetes, established CVD, sleep apnoea or MASH codes, with BMI ≥35 and lifestyle-programme prerequisites. Rough split of 27.5M users: public obesity 4.5M; public diabetes/CV ~7M; commercial (mostly diabetes/cardiac codes) ~8M; cash ~7.5M; gray ~0.5M. The 503B exclusion was finalised in 2027 and compounders are marginal. The gray market is now mostly personal-import Indian generic pens by mail, which FDA and CBP interdict only intermittently. Oral share of new starts has passed 50%; weekly injectables still lead total volume among long-term users.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics; now approved 6+)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide, Nov 2027, with bone-age and growth monitoring postmarketing requirement)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: phase 3 AUD trials of oral semaglutide under way, no approval; addiction clinics prescribe off-label, and it is widely reported
microdosing and 'maintenance dosing' at sub-therapeutic doses to limit flatness and lean-mass loss
scheduled 'drug holidays' (weekends, holidays, before events), now common and tolerated by prescribers though not labelled
craving reduction for nicotine and gambling, still observational
drugs.pipeline_note: No new class reached the US market this step. CagriSema: FDA complete response letter Dec 2026 (efficacy margin vs existing therapy and manufacturing questions); Novo plans to resubmit in 2029. Retatrutide: Lilly filed its BLA in Mar 2027. In Feb 2028 FDA asked for more bone-mineral-density and dysesthesia data and called an advisory committee, which extended the review; decision now expected H1 2029. Amycretin: phase 3, readouts 2029. Survodutide: filed Oct 2028, decision no earlier than late 2029. MariTide (monthly): phase 3. Bimagrumab and other muscle-preserving adjuncts: phase 2/3. After the bone findings, FDA now wants DXA endpoints in incretin phase 3 programmes.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and still the leading cause of discontinuation. Drug holidays cause GI symptoms to return at each restart.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; 2027 label language advises re-titration after interruptions of more than two weeks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal confirmation in long-term data; absolute risk low.

Now treated as a population problem. In claims-linked cohorts, users 65+ on drug for more than two years lose grip strength and gait speed measurably faster than matched non-users; sarcopenia diagnoses in on-drug older adults are up roughly 30% relative.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2027 class labelling recommends resistance training and protein counselling; Medicare Bridge requires a documented strength/nutrition plan for 65+ enrollees.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fractures
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Pooled DXA data show 1.5–2.5% hip BMD loss in the first 18 months, greater in women over 60. A large 2027 Medicare cohort found ~1.3× hip-fracture risk in users 65+ beyond two years of use. The absolute excess is a few fractures per 1,000 patient-years and is concentrated in the frail.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA safety communication and class label update (Jul 2027); baseline DXA recommended for 65+ and postmenopausal women; Medicare covers screening DXA at initiation; postmarketing bone studies required for all products.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort data still conflict; a 2027 meta-analysis found a small elevated risk with wide confidence intervals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA added NAION to the postmarketing adverse-reactions section in 2027, with no boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in subsequent data.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Two 2027–28 patient-reported-outcome surveys put 'noticeably flattened enjoyment' at 12–20% of long-term users, dose-dependent and usually reversible with dose reduction or interruption. No RCT has measured it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested anhedonia/hedonic-tone instruments in ongoing AUD and next-generation trials; there is no label language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world regain is now better characterised: roughly half of lost weight is regained within 12 months, more after abrupt stops. Cycling users show stepwise regain, with lean mass recovering more slowly than fat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy coverage arguments.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Low vitamin D, B12 and protein intake are common in users, and their role in the bone findings is debated.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Endocrine Society guidance recommends nutrition screening; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents and now children 6–11 who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still no data past ~6 years. Pediatric growth, puberty-timing and peak-bone-mass questions have become specific concerns since the bone findings.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric liraglutide approval carries a 10-year registry requirement covering growth and bone age.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Compounded harms are falling since the 503B exclusion; reports now come mainly from personal-import and counterfeit pens.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised 2027; import alerts on unapproved semaglutide.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Novo Nordisk did not submit an internal DXA substudy analysis showing BMD loss in older trial participants to FDA in a timely way, and did not publish it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DOJ and FDA investigations; Senate HELP hearing (Nov 2027); FDA audit of incretin trial data packages; litigation pending.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks is still declining slowly. Because more people are off the drug, losses are smaller than 2026 forecasts. Protein and calcium/vitamin D fortification ('bone-smart') is the new callout after the 2027 safety news. A countertrend has appeared: premium 'full-fat, full-portion' products are marketed as unmedicated indulgence.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume is still sliding, about 2–3% a year in the US. The heaviest-drinking decile keeps shrinking, and off-label AUD prescribing reinforces this. Drug holidays have created a weekend spike in premium purchases, which brands now target.

restaurants.state: Traffic is stable. A split has opened: small-plate concepts serve on-drug diners, while affluent coastal neighbourhoods see a revival of large-format, 'eat-it-all' dining as a status display.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are still contracting but more slowly as some users regain. Size volatility from cycling is real enough that adjustable and stretch fits are a merchandising category. Athleisure that shows muscle is gaining.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth segment. Physicians refer patients to gyms after the bone/muscle label update; Medicare Advantage plans add resistance-training benefits; small-group strength studios are expanding fastest in Sunbelt suburbs.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is at 44% and shrinking. Remaining coverage is concentrated on diabetes and cardiac codes, with stricter prior authorisation. Public payers are absorbing the obesity population at fixed prices. Pharmacy trend is moderating to ~8% as unit prices fall.

pharma.state: Revenue is still growing, but price falls offset volume. Lilly leads US share on tirzepatide and Foundayo. Novo is weakened by the CagriSema CRL, the data scandal, an ex-US generics squeeze and leadership turnover. Investors now treat the global incretin market at the lower end of the $150B-by-2030 forecasts.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among people under 50, a thin body now mostly signals 'on it, and probably on the $149 pill.' It no longer reads as discipline. Visible muscle and evident appetite have become the signals of resources and time.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness is cheap and widespread, including through public programmes, and has lost value as a class marker. The scarce ideal is muscular, well-fed 'unmedicated vitality': trainers, protein, sleep and time. It is most visible among affluent women 25–40 in Los Angeles and New York, who borrow bodybuilding's 'natty' language. The middle third, who lost employer coverage, are the ones most often cycling.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Public eating with appetite has become a status performance on coastal social media ('finish-the-plate' videos). Drug-holiday meals (Thanksgiving, weddings, anniversaries) are planned weeks in advance. School lunch staff report on-drug teenagers barely eating.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles in some cities list 'off it' or 'holidaying' as signals. Couples coordinate drug holidays around trips and anniversaries. Libido complaints are discussed openly and are a common reason for dose reduction.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is being revalued. It is treatable, but it is also now read as vitality and as evidence of being 'yourself'. 'Food noise' still means something to silence, while 'hunger' is becoming something to show.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Surveys estimate 12–20% of long-term users notice flattened enjoyment. Prescribers routinely offer step-down doses. Telehealth platforms sell 'holiday-friendly' titration plans. 'The flats' is common slang.
interior_life.framing: A side effect you manage, like a sedating antihistamine. Addiction medicine still frames the same effect as treatment, and some users call it relief.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Managers in sales and creative fields report a few staff saying they lost drive; others report better focus without snacking. Employers stay out of it because they have mostly stopped paying for the drug. No employer encourages use.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians joke about audiences 'on the flats'. Some writers schedule drug holidays to write. Extreme flavours (sour, spicy, bitter) and loud, high-stimulus leisure stay popular with users seeking a reward signal.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is a recognised and openly discussed reason for dose changes. Couples therapists list it as a routine intake question.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The US–India price gap and the coverage squeeze on the middle third are 2028 campaign talking points. Pundits use 'Ozempic electorate' as a jibe about apathy, but there is no evidence that turnout or engagement changed.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access but more cautious on safety. The bone/muscle class label, the CagriSema CRL and the retatrutide review extension show an FDA rebuilding credibility after the Novo data scandal. Enforcement against compounders is complete.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: the Medicare Bridge has been extended as a CMMI model through 2030; Medicaid opt-in at $245 in 24 states; free oral GLP-1 through HRSA community health centres ($149 federal purchase price, $4B appropriated FY2028–29). There is no mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Public coverage is conditioned on BMI/comorbidity, a documented strength-and-nutrition plan for 65+ and baseline DXA. HRSA programme enrolees attend quarterly visits. Adherence is not monitored beyond refill data.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD keeps GLP-1s off the accession waiver list. Recruiters report applicants who lost weight on the drug and are rejected over regain risk and missing records. The question is under review.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US-versus-world price gap is wider: India $6–40, US cash $149–299. Manufacturers' price concessions remain tied to tariff relief. Personal import of Indian pens is a tolerated nuisance and not yet a policy fight.

events.event: FDA issues complete response letter for Novo Nordisk's CagriSema, citing an insufficient efficacy margin and manufacturing questions; no new incretin class will reach the US market before 2029

Medicare cohort study links more than two years of GLP-1 use in adults 65+ to accelerated hip bone loss and ~1.3× hip-fracture risk; FDA issues a class safety communication and label update recommending baseline DXA and resistance training

Whistleblower documents show Novo Nordisk did not submit an internal DXA bone-density analysis from a semaglutide trial in older adults to FDA in a timely way; DOJ opens a probe, Novo shares fall ~25% and the CEO departs within weeks
FDA extends liraglutide approval (Saxenda and generics) to children aged 6–11 with obesity, attaching a 10-year growth and bone-age registry requirement
Employer benefits survey: only 44% of large employers now cover GLP-1s for weight management, down from 60%; most remaining plans restrict coverage to diabetes, cardiovascular and sleep-apnoea codes
FY2028 appropriations fund a $4B HRSA programme providing free oral GLP-1s at community health centres at a $149 federal purchase price, as CMS extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2030

open_tensions: The middle third is being squeezed: employer retreat pushes the insured middle off the drug while public programmes cover the poor and old and cash covers the rich. The 'missing middle' is a live 2028 campaign issue with no fix yet.

The bone and muscle findings collide with the policy push. Medicare is expanding long-term use in the population most exposed to fracture risk, and children 6–11 now start a drug whose effect on peak bone mass is unknown.

After the Novo data scandal, trust in manufacturer safety data is damaged while FDA weighs retatrutide's 28% efficacy against its bone and dysesthesia questions. Many expect that decision to set the terms for every next-generation drug.
Thinness has lost status value while drug holidays become routine. The population is cycling more on purpose, and nobody has measured what deliberate cycling does to lean mass, bone or mood.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Orals (Wegovy pill and Foundayo) are still offered at $149/month starting doses through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
Medicare still pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay for obesity coverage under the GLP-1 Bridge terms.
Indian generic semaglutide still sells for single- to low-double-digit dollars per month, and Canada still has approved generic semaglutide.
Suicidal ideation remains debunked and off the labels of Wegovy, Saxenda and Zepbound.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: the $149 pill, the missing middle, and why the new status symbol is a woman who finishes her plate
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2028 about one American adult in ten takes an incretin drug. Two years earlier it was about one in nine. The headline number hides how much the user base has changed. Roughly seventeen million adults have taken the drugs and are off them now. Nearly a third of everyone who has ever started has stopped at least once and come back. Most stopped because their employer did, not because of side effects. Only 44 percent of large employers still cover weight management, down from 60 percent in 2026. The plans that remain cover diabetes, heart disease and sleep apnoea, behind BMI thresholds and prior-authorisation forms that benefits managers privately call deterrents.

The state has moved into part of that gap. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was meant to end in December 2027. Instead it has become a demonstration model running to 2030, still paying $245 a month with a $50 copay, for about 2.4 million older Americans. Twenty-four states have opted their Medicaid programmes in at the same price. Since April, community health centres funded by a $4 billion federal appropriation have handed out daily oral GLP-1s free to uninsured adults with severe obesity. Washington buys those pills at $149 a month. Brand prices have come down in steps without collapsing: $149 to start, $199 to $299 to stay on, through TrumpRx and the manufacturers' direct sites. In India the same molecule costs less than a lunch. A pen ordered from Pune by mail is the country's mildest form of smuggling. The result has two tiers that do not line up with income in a simple way. The poor and the old are increasingly covered, and the rich pay cash. Teachers, dental hygienists and warehouse supervisors whose plans dropped coverage either pay out of pocket, cycle on and off, or stop.

The safety story of the period is about bone. In July 2027 a Medicare cohort linked more than two years of use after age 65 to faster hip bone loss and about a third more hip fractures. The absolute excess was a few per thousand patient-years. It was still enough for a class label change, baseline bone scans and a strength-training plan as a condition of Medicare coverage. Two months later, documents reached reporters showing that Novo Nordisk had not submitted an internal bone-density analysis from an older-adult trial to the FDA in a timely way. The chief executive left, the Justice Department opened a probe, and the FDA has been more cautious since. It rejected CagriSema, extended Lilly's retatrutide review, and now asks for bone scans in every trial. No new drug class reached the market in these two years. The one major approval was old liraglutide, extended in November 2027 to children aged six to eleven, with a ten-year registry to track how they grow.

The culture has moved faster than the pharmacology. A thin body no longer signals discipline when a federally funded clinic hands out the pill. In Los Angeles and Manhattan the expensive look among women in their late twenties and thirties is muscle, sleep and visible appetite, which they call 'natty' or 'unmedicated'. Strength studios in suburban Phoenix and Atlanta take referrals from doctors. Restaurants serve two markets: small plates for people on the drug, and large showy portions for people who want to be seen eating.

The flattening that people called 'Ozempic personality' in 2026 is now just 'the flats': a known complaint, discussed with doctors, managed by lowering the dose. Drug holidays have become routine. People come off for Thanksgiving, for weddings, for anniversaries, for the novel they have been meaning to finish. Each time nausea returns at restart, and each cycle regains some fat faster than muscle. Nobody has measured what a decade of deliberate cycling does to the body.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renee Kowalczyk sets two alarms on Fridays. The first is for work. The second, at 7:40, reminds her not to take the Foundayo.

She is forty-six and a billing coordinator at an orthopaedic group in Toledo. Her plan dropped weight coverage last January. A letter from benefits used the word 'realignment'. Now she pays LillyDirect $249 a month, and the money comes out the same day as the car payment. Weekends off stretch the bottle, and they also bring Saturdays back.

At work she enters codes for hip fractures. She notices the birth years. She doesn't say anything about it.

At lunch her coworker Dani eats a full Italian sub at her desk and films the last bite. Dani has never been on anything, and she makes sure people know it.

After work Renee picks up her mother, who is seventy-three, from the bone scan Medicare required before her refill. Her mother pays fifty dollars a month for Wegovy and now has a sheet of resistance-band exercises taped to the fridge. In the car she asks whether 'osteopenia' means the bad one. Renee tells her it means the beginning of the bad one.

At home her son Theo, nine, is eating cereal out of the box. The pediatrician mentioned liraglutide at his checkup and used the word 'registry'. Renee hasn't decided.

On Saturday morning she wakes up hungry and it feels like weather coming back. She makes pancakes for real and eats three. She cries a little over the third, and isn't sure why. On Monday she'll take the pill, and the nausea will come back with it.

least_plausible_claims.why: 0.9% of ~73M under-18s is roughly 650k children on drug. The 2026 base was ~0.6% of children with obesity, with under-12 use now only ~40k, so this implies an implausibly large jump in two years with no mechanism or reconciliation. Fails magnitude and mechanism.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Among people under 50, a thin body now mostly signals 'on it, and probably on the $149 pill.'
least_plausible_claims.why: The candidate's own age bands have only 4% of 18–29s and 9% of 30–49s on the drug. Most thin people under 50 are therefore not on it, so thinness cannot mostly signal drug use. This is an asserted cultural shift that contradicts the population figures. Fails mechanism.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Off-drug population: ~17M former users, most of whom stopped over cost or coverage, not side effects
least_plausible_claims.why: The starting world has GI effects as the leading cause of discontinuation and ~two-thirds of starters stopping within a year. Employer coverage fell only 16 points among large employers. The claim that most of 17M stopped over coverage is asserted, not derived. Fails mechanism.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder but recognisable society. The 'missing middle' loses employer coverage and cycles on and off the drug, older users face a hip-fracture signal (~1.3× in 65+ beyond two years), and children 6–11 now start a drug with unknown effects on peak bone mass. Offsets are public programmes (Bridge, HRSA, Medicaid), a sharp FDA response and an openly discussed 'flats' complaint, so the harm is measured and nameable. Inequality and public health score highest; epistemic is moderate because manufacturer trust is damaged but the signals are being measured.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is realised and traceable. Adoption is 10.5 (-0.5), employer coverage is 44%, liraglutide 6–11 is approved, the bone/muscle wave and Novo scandal appear as events, no new class launches, HRSA and Medicare subsidies are in place, 'the flats' is mainstream, and aesthetic inversion shows in the culture fields. mechanism: most chains are shown (coverage retreat to middle-third cycling, bone data to label to Medicare conditions), but the claims on thinness signalling, why former users stopped, and the retatrutide review stretching to H1 2029 are asserted. magnitude: adults on drug, ever-used, income, age and cycled shares all fit the envelope and reconcile. Medicare 2.4M + Medicaid 1.5M + HRSA 0.6M = 4.5M; 2.4M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.1B and the other dollar figures check; the 27.5M user split sums. The 0.9% pediatric figure is not reconciled with ~40k under-12s or the 2026 base, and the cash price high of $299 sits oddly beside 'nominal list prices persist'.
rationale.generativity: The Renee Kowalczyk vignette gives scenes and texture: the Friday alarm, the cost of Foundayo against the car payment, coding hip fractures, the coworker filming her sub, the mother's bone scan and resistance-band sheet, and the son and the 'registry'. The world fields add drug-holiday meals, dating-profile signals and 'finish-the-plate' videos. It is rich and film-ready, with several implied characters and settings.

least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 0.9% of ~73M under-18s is about 660k children. The start world had roughly 0.6% of children with obesity on the drug, so this is close to an order-of-magnitude jump in two years. With only ~40k under 12, it implies ~620k adolescents, and no mechanism or arithmetic is shown.

mechanism: the HRSA programme is funded in Apr 2028 and is said to have 0.6M enrolees within nine months, all at community health centres. No ramp-up chain is shown, and the figure is conveniently what makes the public obesity fill count reach exactly 4.5M.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Among people under 50, a thin body now mostly signals 'on it, and probably on the $149 pill.'
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism and magnitude: with ~10% of adults on the drug (4% of 18–29s), most thin people are not medicated. A majority reading of thinness as drug-induced within two years, and the rapid class inversion of its status, is asserted rather than shown.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder society with identifiable new losers rather than a catastrophe. It has a squeezed middle third (employer retreat, 44% coverage), a bone and muscle burden in the frail 65+ (1.3× hip-fracture risk, `safety_ledger` bone entry), 12–20% reward flattening, and children 6–11 started on a drug with unknown bone effects. Inequality scores highest because of the three-tier access split. The Novo data scandal damages trust in manufacturer safety data. Public subsidy and a label response keep it from going higher.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events: adoption at 10.5, managed price decline to $149–299, employer coverage 60→44, the liraglutide 6–11 approval, the bone and muscle wave, no new class, the Novo scandal, aesthetic inversion, HRSA and Medicare subsidy, and mainstream 'the flats'. The pipeline filings (retatrutide, survodutide) respect the approval rules. mechanism: most chains are shown (coverage loss to cycling, bone cohort to label to Medicare conditions, scandal to FDA caution). Some are asserted: the near-instant status inversion of thinness and the 0.6M HRSA enrolment (claims 2 and 3), plus routine drug holidays and a fast 2027 fracture cohort. magnitude: all headline figures sit inside the envelope (10.5, ever 17, no US generic), and spending, user and public-fill arithmetic reconciles (2.4M×245×12≈$7.1B, 4.5M/27.5M≈16%, 6.5% off-now≈17M). The main flaw is the unexplained jump to 0.9% pediatric use (claim 1). The age-band population shares (20% aged 18–29) are also a little off.
rationale.generativity: The world is rich in scenes: drug-holiday meals, 'finish-the-plate' videos, dating profiles reading 'holidaying', DXA scans, strength studios and 'the flats' as slang. The Renee Kowalczyk vignette shows rather than explains, with its 7:40 alarm, the LillyDirect payment next to the car payment, the coworker filming her sub, the mother's resistance-band sheet and Theo with the cereal box. Characters and conflicts (the missing middle, a mother-daughter bone scan, a pediatric decision) are implied and filmable.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Most stopped because their employer did, not because of side effects.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the same world's safety ledger calls GI effects 'the leading cause of discontinuation'. Employer coverage fell only from 60% to 44% of large employers, and commercial users are a minority of the roughly 17M former users. 'Most stopped over cost' is asserted without a chain and conflicts with the ledger.

Magnitude and mechanism: 0.9% of about 73M under-18s is roughly 650k children. The 2026 baseline was a few tenths of a percent of children with obesity, and only adolescents 12+ were approved. The note offers no ramp that explains a near-order-of-magnitude rise.

Mechanism: the HRSA programme starts in April 2028 through community health centres, yet is shown at 0.6M free-pill enrollees by year-end. No capacity or outreach chain is given for standing up that many patients in about eight months.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder, with new losers but also real offsets. Bone and muscle harm to older adults (1.3x hip-fracture risk, sarcopenia up about 30%), a squeezed middle third, 6–11-year-olds on a long-horizon drug, and a damaged trust in manufacturer data (Novo scandal) drive the score. Thinness becoming cheap and public coverage reaching the poor and old limit severity. The flattening complaint reaches 12–20% of long-term users and is mostly reversible, and drug holidays are normalised without anyone measuring their effects.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events or fields, including the -0.5pp adoption change, employer retreat 60→44%, the under-12 liraglutide approval, the bone wave, the Novo scandal, aesthetic inversion, subsidy and mainstream 'flats'.
